newsitem.title: TUNISIA: Tunusia phosphates output hits record in 1996.
newsitem.headline: Tunusia phosphates output hits record in 1996.

text.p: Major phosphates exporter Tunisia increased its marketable phosphates output in 1996 by 13.7 percent to 7.167 million tonnes from 6.302 million tonnes in 1995, official figures showed on Friday.
"This is an historical record," the century-old state-controlled Compagnie des Phosphates de Gafsa (CPG), which extracts phosphates in the North African country, says in a report obtained by Reuters.
"Increased production was boosted by the recovery that began in 1994 on the world market prices," the report added.
CPG says it was the fifth phosphates producer in the world. Average production was around six million tonnes yearly during the last ten years.

Value of raw phosphates and phosphate by-products exports were estimated to rose by 18 percent for 1996 compared to the previous year, official reports said. No figure for the value was released yet. In 1995, exports of these products, a major foreign exchange earner, were worth 534.1 million dinars ($501.2 million).

Most of the raw phosphates output is sold to the state-controlled firm Groupe Chimique Tunisien (GCT) which has four processing centers in southern Tunisia. GCT exports some 90 percent of its production, mainly fertilisers, and the remaining 10 percent is for the domestic market.
Among Tunisias main clients for by-products are India, China Western Europe, Middle eastern countries.

Official reports said that Tunisia was planning a new fertilisers plant in the southern city of Gabes with a Chinese and Libyan participation in the investment put at 55 million dinars. The plant would produce diammonium phosphate (DAP).
CPG has a 284 million dinars capital and GCT a capital of 238 million dinars. Both of them are chaired by Rabah Dekhil.

Industry officials said CPG had moved in 1996 to profit for the first time thanks to higher fertilisers prices, and a restructuring programme that started in 1992 supported by a 153 million dinars refinancing by the state.
Tunisia's reserves of phosphates are officially estimated at 350 million tonnes. ($=1.06 dinar) Tunis newsroom, 2161-787538
